identifier: M. Kelidou, M. Fazelzadeh, B. Parage, M. van Dijk, T. Hooijschuur, S. Jabbari-Farouji, "Active string fluids and gels formed by dipolar active Brownian particles in 3D", Journal of Chemical Physics 161, 104904 (2024). DOI 10.1063/5.0215545. Values entered come from Sec. II B (units and parameters), Sec. III (state diagram) and Sec. IV-V text.
delivered_by: the person, as the publisher's PDF in ~/Downloads on the MacBook, named in task 039. Fifteen pages including the appendix (Figs. 18-19); the supplementary movies are online only.
publication_status: PEER REVIEWED, CHECKED ON THE FILE. Typeset version of record: submitted 24 April 2024, accepted 23 August 2024, published online 13 September 2024.
grade_rule: E3, grade_tag peer_reviewed. Every result is a claim about the MODEL: three-dimensional overdamped active Brownian spheres with a WCA core and a point magnetic dipole parallel to the propulsion direction, no hydrodynamics. The authors map their parameter ranges onto magnetotactic bacteria only roughly, and no entry carries that mapping as a fact about bacteria.
license_note: Open access under CC BY-NC 4.0. Identifier, stated conditions and numbers only; nothing of the text, figures or movies is reproduced.
method_as_stated: MODEL: N spheres of diameter sigma, each with a point dipole of magnitude mu along its orientation e and an active force of constant magnitude along the same e; WCA repulsion of strength epsilon cut at 2^(1/6) sigma plus the full point dipole-dipole interaction. Overdamped translational and rotational Langevin equations with Dt = kT/gamma_t and Dr = kT/gamma_r; no hydrodynamic interactions. UNITS: length sigma, time tau = 1/Dr, energy kT. Dimensionless parameters: dipolar coupling lambda = mu^2/(kT sigma^3), reduced active force f_a = Fa sigma/kT, reduced density rho* = rho sigma^3, with epsilon* = 1 and gamma_t* = 3; the self-propulsion speed va = Fa/(sigma Dr gamma_t) is identical to the usual Peclet number and equals f_a/3. DENSITIES: rho* = 0.02 and 0.15, packing fraction pi rho*/6 = 0.010 and 0.08. RANGES: 1 <= lambda <= 16 and 0 <= f_a <= 200 at rho* = 0.02; 1 <= lambda <= 12.25 and 0 <= f_a <= 150 at rho* = 0.15. ENGINE: most runs in HOOMD-blue on GPU (version not stated), cubic periodic box, time step 2e-4 tau, N = 8,788 (box length 76.02 at rho* = 0.02). The dipolar interaction is summed without an Ewald correction; the authors justify this where the largest dipolar energy at half the box length stays below 1e-3 (all lambda at rho* = 0.02, lambda <= 6.25 at rho* = 0.15) and confirmed it with a few LAMMPS runs that included Ewald and k-space corrections and gave identical pair distribution functions. A 19,652-particle system (box 99.42) gave the same g(r) at rho* = 0.02, lambda = 16 and was used for structure factors. The rho* = 0.15 runs with 9 <= lambda <= 12.25 used LAMMPS with full Ewald summation and 10,648 particles. PROTOCOL: passive systems equilibrated first from an FCC lattice with random orientations at mu* = 1, then step by step to larger moments (block averaging), then activity raised gradually from f_a = 0 (to 200 at lambda = 16); steady state when the polymerised fraction and the largest-cluster fraction stop drifting and the run exceeds the self-intermediate-scattering relaxation time; runs to steady state of 100 to 1e4 tau, then production of 100 to 1e4 tau. At lambda >= 12.25 with f_a = 0 and 10 the dynamics is too slow to equilibrate within the runs. ANALYSIS: neighbours within 1.2 sigma (first g(r) minimum at rho* = 0.02); rings, chains and branched clusters by neighbour count; states classified as gas (polymerised fraction below 0.5), string fluid (above 0.5 with largest-cluster fraction below 0.7) and percolated network (largest-cluster fraction 0.7 or more).
not_entered: The boundary lines f_a^t0(lambda) and f_a^t1(lambda) of the state diagram as values: they exist only as Fig. 3 curves. The mean-field estimate for f_a^t1 (the head-to-tail dipole force 6 lambda/r_nn^4 at the nearest-neighbour distance) is a formula the paper uses to rationalise the line and is in the note. Structure-factor exponents (0.97 and 0.87), stretching exponents (about 0.81 to 0.28), the subdiffusive exponent 0.72, and the rotational-diffusion enhancement (about twice isolated particles): model detail kept in the note, not a regime boundary. The magnetotactic-bacteria mapping (roughly 0.1 < lambda < 20 and 5 < f_a < 200 from sizes 2-10 um, moments 1e-16 to 1e-14 A m^2 and speeds 10-100 um/s): the authors' rough conversion assuming spheres, not a measurement.
note: The reduced active force f_a is the same dimensionless quantity as Hofmann et al.'s F0 sigma/kT (src_hofmann_2026_frictional_contacts); both are filed under one name for that reason.
